clue.text: A fancy thing leader demolished in passing reference

indicators.note: the 'leader' of ILLUSION is its first letter, and demolishing it knocks that I away

blocks.note: a fancy thing is an ILLUSION; without its first letter it is LLUSION

explanation.surface: Someone mentions, in passing, a fancy building whose owner has been pulled down from power.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fancy' is a noun here (a flight of the imagination), so 'fancy thing' is an illusion, not an ornate object.
explanation.definitionFit: An allusion is a passing reference to something not named outright.

clue.text: Country girl in dance drinking water

indicators.note: the dance takes the water in, so PEE ends up inside BOP

blocks.note: to pass water is to pee

explanation.surface: A girl from the countryside at a dance, sipping only water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Water' is not something drunk but the colloquial kind that is passed: PEE.
explanation.definitionFit: Little Bo Peep, the nursery-rhyme shepherdess who lost her sheep, is a country girl.

clue.text: Cleric is one getting on – change needed

blocks.note: Rev, short for Reverend, a clergyman

explanation.surface: An ageing clergyman is told it is time for a change.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One getting on' looks like an old person; it is I with ON added after it.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: revising a text or plan means changing it, and the result is the change.

clue.text: More reasonable fliers heading up, suppressing anger

indicators.note: in a down clue, going up the grid reads a word from bottom to top
the fliers hold the anger down inside them

blocks.note: the Royal Air Force, Britain's fliers

explanation.surface: Calmer pilots take off while keeping their temper in check.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fliers' are not birds but British airmen, the Royal Air Force; in a down entry 'heading up' reverses them.
explanation.definitionFit: Fairer is the comparative of fair, meaning more reasonable or just.

clue.text: British award for democratic process

explanation.surface: A British honour given out for services to democracy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Award' reads as a noun (a prize) but works as the verb ALLOT.
explanation.definitionFit: Voting by secret paper slips is how democracies choose, so the word names the process itself.

clue.text: Advice to travellers in car? Say nothing!

explanation.walkthrough: 'Belt up!' is British slang for 'be quiet!', as well as the road-safety instruction to buckle your seat belt.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses are commands, matching the imperatives in the clue.

clue.text: Fellow clothed in colour put back in custody

indicators.note: a fellow clothed in a colour is wrapped in it, so the colour goes round him

explanation.surface: A man dressed in bright clothes is sent back to the cells.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads like prison clothing, but the colour is simply the outer layer of letters wrapped round the fellow.
explanation.definitionFit: To remand a defendant is to send them back into custody pending trial.

clue.text: Period lacking a horrible inadequate ruler

indicators.note: a word lacking a letter A simply goes without it, so the A is removed
NASTY falls short by its last letter

blocks.note: a day is a period; without A it is DY
horrible = NASTY, cut short to NAST

explanation.surface: A monarch who is both cruel and incompetent, at some point in history.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Period' tempts you toward ERA or AGE; the one that loses an A cleanly is DAY.
explanation.definitionFit: A dynast is a ruler, especially a member of a hereditary ruling family.

clue.text: Female in business arrangement with what’s charged amounting to a financial crime

indicators.note: the female is in the business arrangement, placed inside its letters

blocks.note: a deal is a business arrangement
a cation is a positively charged ion

explanation.surface: A woman in a business deal overcharges and ends up guilty of fraud.
explanation.walkthrough: 'What's charged' sounds like a fee, but it is chemistry: a cation is an ion with a positive electric charge.
explanation.definitionFit: Defalcation is the misappropriation of funds held in trust, a financial crime.

clue.text: Nameless tribe to employ a few words

indicators.note: N is the abbreviation for name, so a nameless CLAN loses its N

blocks.note: a tribe is a CLAN; without N (name) it is CLA

explanation.surface: An unknown tribe that communicates in very few words.
explanation.walkthrough: N for name is a standard abbreviation, so 'nameless' tells you to drop an N.
explanation.definitionFit: A clause is a short group of words, part of a sentence or document.

clue.text: Traveller and female relation hiding in shed

indicators.note: the relation hides inside the shed, so her letters sit within it

blocks.note: to shed (light, heat) is to emit

explanation.surface: A traveller and a grandmother are hiding out in a garden shed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shed' is the verb, as in shedding heat: EMIT, which then holds GRAN.
explanation.definitionFit: An emigrant is someone who travels away from their home country to settle elsewhere.

clue.text: Language, one set right to left

indicators.note: in an across answer, reading right to left turns the letters round

blocks.note: to set something down is to put it

explanation.surface: A script in which each word is written from right to left, as in Arabic or Hebrew.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Set' is the verb PUT; I PUT, read backwards, gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by class: it is an indigenous tongue of Brazil, once widely spoken along the coast.

clue.text: Wandering as a pilgrim, using someone else’s words

definitions.note: a gerund phrase for the noun: plagiarism is the using of someone else's words

indicators.note: a wandering pilgrim's letters stray out of order

explanation.surface: A pilgrim on the road recites prayers composed by someone else.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wandering as a pilgrim' reads like a description of travel; 'as a' belongs to the fodder, not the sentence.
explanation.definitionFit: Plagiarism is passing off someone else's words as your own.

clue.text: Branch of Christianity sending out manic signal when in trouble

indicators.note: letters in trouble are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: A church in crisis broadcasting a frantic distress call.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface paints a mayday; the 'manic signal' is simply eleven letters to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Anglicanism is the Church of England and its sister churches, a branch of Christianity.

clue.text: European article in medical journal shows marine animal

indicators.note: an article printed in a journal sits inside it, so LE goes within LANCET

blocks.note: The Lancet, the British medical journal

explanation.surface: A paper by a European in a medical journal reveals a new sea creature.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Article' is a grammatical article, not a paper: LE is the French word for 'the', and The Lancet is the famous British medical journal.
explanation.definitionFit: A lancelet (amphioxus) is a small fish-like marine animal.

clue.text: Malicious gossip when nothing’s found in that special box

indicators.note: the O is found inside the gossip, sitting within its letters

explanation.surface: Spiteful gossip about a box that turns out to be empty.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition sits at the end and is vague on purpose; 'nothing's found in' reads as 'the box is empty' but puts O inside SLANDER.
explanation.definitionFit: A solander is a book-shaped protective box for prints or botanical specimens, named after the botanist Daniel Solander.

clue.text: Tailless bird had, in short, to be a hoax

indicators.note: the bird loses its tail, its last letter
'had' in short is the contraction 'd

blocks.note: had shortened to 'd, as in I'd

explanation.surface: A bird with no tail turns out to be a fake.
explanation.walkthrough: Canard is also French for duck, which makes a bird in the wordplay a neat touch.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: the word, borrowed from French, means a false story spread to deceive.

clue.text: Goddess at one time protected by road team

indicators.note: something protected by a team is surrounded by it, so THEN sits between the two As

blocks.note: the AA, the Automobile Association, Britain's roadside rescue service

explanation.surface: A goddess who once had a roadside patrol to protect her.
explanation.walkthrough: The AA (Automobile Association) is a British motoring organisation whose patrols rescue broken-down drivers, hence 'road team'.
explanation.definitionFit: Athena is the Greek goddess of wisdom and war.

clue.text: Construed as ‘ancient’, a biblical people

indicators.note: to construe is to interpret, so the letters are read in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A people from the Bible interpreted as simply 'ancient'.
explanation.walkthrough: The trailing 'a' looks like part of the definition, but it is the last letter of the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: The Canaanites were the people of Canaan in the Old Testament.

clue.text: Piece of land not good over time – too hot, maybe

indicators.note: G is the abbreviation for good, so the G comes out
in a down answer, one piece placed over another comes first

blocks.note: a GARDEN is a piece of land; without G it is ARDEN

explanation.surface: A patch of land left fallow over a summer that was far too hot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Maybe' flags that the definition is an example: ardent literally means burning.
explanation.definitionFit: Ardent means burning or glowing, and figuratively fervent or passionate, so possibly too hot.

clue.text: Enlightenment men found in fiery ritual once

indicators.note: the men are found in the ritual, standing inside its letters

blocks.note: sati (suttee), the former Hindu practice of a widow burning on her husband's pyre
OR, 'other ranks', soldiers who are not officers

explanation.surface: Men who claim to have reached enlightenment through an old fire ceremony.
explanation.walkthrough: OR for 'other ranks' is the usual way to turn 'men' into two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Satori is the sudden enlightenment sought in Zen Buddhism.

clue.text: First item under the hammer making money in Africa

blocks.note: each numbered item sold at an auction is catalogued as one
I = one, the Roman numeral: lot one is the first

explanation.surface: The opening lot at an auction fetches a good price in Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: At auction the first item is Lot I; 'first' becomes the numeral I, placed after LOT as in a catalogue.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: it is the currency of Lesotho, a small kingdom inside South Africa.

clue.text: City somehow in good taste, not OTT

indicators.note: the letters O, T and T are taken out of the phrase
the remaining letters come together in some other way

blocks.note: IN GOOD TASTE minus O, T, T

explanation.surface: A city with tasteful style that never goes over the top.
explanation.walkthrough: OTT (over the top) reads as a comment on taste, but its letters are what gets removed.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: it is a large port city in southern California.

clue.text: Romantic present

blocks.note: romantic in the sense of loving and gentle
the verb: to present or formally offer, as a resignation or payment

explanation.walkthrough: 'Present' is a verb here, as in presenting a payment, not a gift.
explanation.definitionFit: Tender means gentle and loving, and to tender is to offer or present formally.

clue.text: I angered a lot, being revolutionary (joint) president

indicators.note: a revolution turns things over, so the letters are overturned

explanation.surface: A former revolutionary leader who admits he angered many people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Revolutionary' suits Ortega, a Sandinista guerrilla leader, so it does double duty as the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Daniel Ortega is president of Nicaragua, since 2025 formally sharing the office with his wife as co-president.

clue.text: See 24
